analysis:
This PR changes documentation only: docs/provider/cli-reference.md (visible tail units at lines 2123-2387 and 2388-2549 are unchanged context; the changed ranges are around 743-769, 1852 and 1859-1860, outside the supplied text) and docs/provider/installation.md (adds a 'Roll back to the previous release' section at head lines 219-256 and bumps the date). No code, controls or configuration are modified, so no control regression is visible.

The docs describe a new `darkbloom update --rollback` flow. It restores the retained predecessor from ~/.darkbloom/recovery/predecessor/ through a journaled swap under the update lease. It drains the provider, quarantines the rolled-back release, requires confirmation (`--yes` is needed without a TTY), contacts no coordinator, and refuses combination with --check-only, --override-quarantine and --coordinator.

The security-relevant questions are for whoever reviews the code, since the code is not supplied here:
1. Does the rollback path re-verify the predecessor's code signature and designated requirement (Team ID SLDQ2GJ6TL) before activation?
2. Does it consult the coordinator's revoked or qualified build state? It contacts no coordinator, so a revoked or unqualified predecessor could be reinstated. The App Attest build qualification and revocation checks (A-017, T-054) would still gate serving authorization, but that is not verifiable here.
3. Does the rollback share T-043's trust assumption, that the watchdog's rollback authority is the same replaceable binary, and is the predecessor directory writable only by the owner?

These are unverified contracts rather than findings. The documentation claims no new trust grants. The quarantine and one-predecessor limits are consistent with the existing update-recovery model. In the supplied tail text I saw nothing that weakens T-053, T-054 or T-041. needs_deeper_review is set so the code behind the rollback (UpdateRollback.swift, UpdateInstallLayout.swift) can be checked for signature verification and revocation handling.
